context: Hiroshi (elder) is babysitting six-year-old Sho. Out of a drawer he pulls a postcard he hasn't looked at in decades — one his own mother wrote to him as a child.
purpose: oral history micro-moment — an old letter becomes a doorway

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: しょうくん、これ、見たことあるかい。
lines.en: Sho-kun — have you seen this before?
lines.style: Holds up the postcard carefully. Voice lower, intimate.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.style: Genuine kid question. Leans in, head tilted.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: はがき。お母さんからの。私の、お母さん。
lines.en: A postcard. From my mother. My mother.
lines.style: Slowly. Three short sentences. Lets the word 「母さん」 mean what it means.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ええ…おじいちゃんの、お母さん…？
lines.style: Genuine kid astonishment. The math doesn't fit at first.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.en: When I was a child too.
lines.style: Quiet, slow. A whole life given as five syllables.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.style: A small precious request. Hands not yet touching the postcard.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: もちろん。ゆっくり読みなさい。時間はある。
lines.en: Of course. Read it slowly. There's time.
lines.style: Slides closer in the voice. The 「時間はある」 is the whole afternoon.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.style: Settles into the side of the older man in the voice. Reads in silence after.
